title: Tuberculosis — WHO baseline (draft)
summary: WHO tuberculosis baseline for primary care: rapid molecular diagnosis, drug-susceptible first-line treatment, TB/HIV co-management, and preventive treatment. National TB programmes refine regimens and DR-TB pathways via overlays. DRAFT — clinician verification required before approval.
diagnosis: Use a WHO-recommended rapid molecular test (e.g. Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra) as the initial diagnostic test, including for rifampicin resistance.
Evaluate for extrapulmonary TB by site; chest X-ray supports but does not replace bacteriological confirmation.
Test all people with TB for HIV.
treatment: Drug-susceptible pulmonary TB (adults): 2 months HRZE intensive phase + 4 months HR continuation (2HRZE/4HR).
A 4-month rifapentine-moxifloxacin regimen is a WHO-recommended alternative in eligible patients.
Use fixed-dose combinations and support adherence (DOT / digital adherence tools).
Rifampicin-resistant / MDR-TB: treat with a WHO-recommended regimen (e.g. BPaLM) under programme conditions — refer.
tbHiv: Start ART in all TB/HIV patients (within 2 weeks; within 8 weeks if not severely immunosuppressed — earlier if CD4 very low, except TB meningitis).
prevention: TB preventive treatment (TPT) for eligible contacts and people living with HIV.
Contact investigation for all people diagnosed with TB.
redFlags: Drug-induced liver injury on TB treatment (jaundice, vomiting) — stop hepatotoxic drugs and reassess.
TB meningitis or miliary TB — urgent referral.
nationalOverlayNotes: Per-country overlays should adopt the national TB programme guidance (regimens, DR-TB pathway, recording/reporting).
